symptom: After the synthetic signature claim was snapshotted once, an older request-drift regression still waited for a second claimedSignerId descriptor read. The intended mutation never fired, so the test failed on its read-count assertion even though both new public-key-swap regressions passed. The failure was a test trigger coupled to an obsolete call sequence, not an evidence-verifier or runner failure.
lesson: A successful hardening that eliminates repeated reads can invalidate adversarial tests that inject mutation on the removed read. This is fixture drift, not proof that the original request-drift guardrail regressed. The CI log identifies the failed descriptor-read-count assertion while both new key-swap negative tests passed.
guardrail: When a test models mutation between validation phases, bind its trigger to a phase boundary that still exists after the refactor (here the later policy-anchor preflight), assert that the mutation actually fired, and separately assert the intended fail-closed blocker. Never weaken or remove the negative security assertion merely to restore green CI.
